title: Enable repo-assistant sessions to use whitelisted GitHub auth from .env.autonomy for live PR reads
specification:
# PRD: Enable repo-assistant sessions to use whitelisted GitHub auth from .env.autonomy for live PR reads

Priority: high

## Problem
Repo-assistant sessions can inspect local files but cannot read live GitHub pull request metadata, review comments, or threads because session startup does not expose authenticated GitHub access and network permissions, even though the project already loads GitHub tokens from `.env.autonomy`.

## Goal
Allow repo-assistant sessions to automatically use a whitelisted GitHub token from `.env.autonomy` at startup so they can read live PR data for the current repository without per-session manual configuration.

## Requirements
- At session launch, load only whitelisted auth env vars such as `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN` from `.env.autonomy` or equivalent runtime secret source.
- Provide repo-assistant sessions outbound GitHub network access limited to required GitHub API endpoints.
- Bind the GitHub tool/plugin in-session using the loaded credential.
- Validate that the credential has read access to the target repository and PR resources before enabling GitHub-backed PR inspection.
- Surface a clear runtime status in the control panel when GitHub access is unavailable, misconfigured, or unauthorized.
- Avoid exposing raw secret values to the assistant transcript, logs, or UI.
- Prefer runtime secret injection over reading arbitrary env files from within the assistant session.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A newly started repo-assistant session for `asalaza6/autonomy-v2` can read live PR metadata for a known PR without manual token entry.
- The session can retrieve PR diff, top-level comments, reviews, and unresolved review threads through the GitHub tools.
- When the token is missing or invalid, the control panel shows a clear failure reason instead of silent fallback.
- Secret values are never displayed in assistant responses or persisted in logs.
- No per-session manager action is required beyond maintaining a valid repo-scoped credential in the approved secret source.

## Verification
- Start a fresh repo-assistant session and confirm it can fetch PR info for `asalaza6/autonomy-v2#27`.
- Verify the session can call PR metadata, diff, comments, reviews, and review-thread reads successfully.
- Test failure cases with missing token, invalid token, and token lacking repo access; confirm user-visible error states.
- Review logs and transcript output to confirm token values are redacted and never exposed.

tasks.title: Enable authenticated GitHub PR reads for repo-assistant sessions using whitelisted runtime secrets
tasks.description: Implement the repo-assistant session startup and control-plane changes needed to inject only whitelisted GitHub auth env vars from the approved runtime secret source, grant the session only the GitHub network access required for PR inspection, bind the in-session GitHub tool/plugin with the injected credential, validate repository and pull-request read access before enabling GitHub-backed inspection, and surface explicit runtime status when access is unavailable or unauthorized without exposing raw token values. Likely touch points include session/runner startup and env shaping under `src/autonomy-v2/runner/` or `src/autonomy-v2/commands/`, control-plane status and UI reporting under `src/autonomy-v2/control-plane/` and `src/server/control-plane/`, GitHub integration/bootstrap paths, and focused unit or smoke coverage for repo-assistant session capability checks.
acceptance: A freshly started repo-assistant session for `asalaza6/autonomy-v2` automatically receives only whitelisted GitHub auth variables such as `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GH_TOKEN` from the approved runtime secret source, without requiring any manual token entry inside the session.

The assistant session does not read arbitrary env files directly for this feature; credential delivery is performed by runtime injection or equivalent pre-session secret shaping controlled by the host process.

When a valid repo-scoped credential is present, the session can use the GitHub tool/plugin to read live PR data for `asalaza6/autonomy-v2#27`, including PR metadata, diff, top-level comments, reviews, and unresolved review threads.

Before GitHub-backed PR inspection is marked available, startup performs a read-access validation against the target repository and PR resources; if validation fails, GitHub inspection remains disabled rather than silently falling back.

Repo-assistant sessions receive outbound network permission only for the GitHub endpoints required to perform the supported PR read operations, and the implementation documents or enforces that narrower allowlist in the relevant runtime configuration.

The control panel or equivalent runtime status surface shows a clear, user-visible state for GitHub access success and for each failure mode tested here: missing token, invalid token, and token lacking repository access.
Raw secret values are never emitted into assistant transcript content, structured status payloads, logs, or UI output; any error or debug reporting uses redacted or non-secret-safe messaging only.

Focused automated coverage exercises successful GitHub capability enablement plus the missing-token, invalid-token, and unauthorized-token failure paths, and the implementation runs `npm run typecheck` along with the relevant control-plane, runner, or smoke tests covering session startup and status reporting.
